summary: The Disaster Inc. Naming Dispute began with one simple truth: Waluigi came up with Disaster Inc. first. It was accurate. It was elegant. It looked good in a case file. Then Archie Miser began calling the group The Freeroamer Heroes, because Archie believes that if a name sounds noble enough it can outrun the property damage behind it. Wario then entered the argument with The Freeloader Zeros, arguing that the party produces zero profit, zero repayment, and zero respect for whoever noticed the loot first. The dispute has since spread to the Liberated Toads, where named survivors such as Rodger, Teacher T, Bully T, Nerd T, and Geek T have started using, analyzing, mocking, or merchandising the rival names. Waluigi considers this brand theft. Archie calls it hope. Wario calls it billable.
description:
Waluigi is documenting this event because history must record not only wars, betrayals, and planar fractures, but also the smaller crimes: like people stealing Waluigi's perfectly good faction name thunder.

Let the record state plainly, before the excuses begin, before Archie composes a speech and Wario prepares an invoice: **Waluigi coined the name Disaster Inc. first.** Everything that follows in this article — the rival brands, the button economy, the usage charts, the courtroom-adjacent theatre — is downstream of that single fact. The Disaster Inc. Naming Dispute is not, as Archie insists, a philosophical debate about the nature of heroism. It is not, as Wario insists, a matter of accounts receivable. It is a theft. A slow, loud, communal theft of a name Waluigi invented, conducted in broad daylight by people who then had the audacity to argue that their version was better.

Waluigi is a fair historian. Waluigi will document every side of this dispute, including the sides that are wrong. But Waluigi will do so from the correct starting position, which is that Waluigi was right and remains right.

## Why This Event Deserves An Article At All


A reader might reasonably ask why an encyclopedia crowded with assassinations, sieges, planar fractures, and world-eating worms should devote space to an argument about what to call a group of adventurers. Waluigi anticipated this objection and has a complete answer.

First: names are not decoration. Names are power. The Iron Legion understood this when they stole the Vigilance and renamed it the "Legionlance," a word so ugly Waluigi suspects it was chosen as a form of psychological warfare. The Peach Loyalists understood it when they built an entire military movement on the single word "Peach." The Mushroom Regency understood it when they chose to be a "Regency" — a placeholder, a caretaker's title — precisely so that no one would ask why the caretakers never gave the house back. In every one of these cases, the name did work that armies could not. To call something is to decide what it is.

Waluigi named the party Disaster Inc. because that is what the party is, and the fight to overwrite that name is a fight over the truth itself.

Second: this dispute is a rare window into the personalities of the people driving the entire crisis. You cannot understand Archie Miser until you understand why he needs the party to be called Heroes. You cannot understand Wario until you understand why he needs them to be called Zeros. And you cannot understand Waluigi — the most objective observer in recorded history — until you understand that Waluigi needs them to be called what they actually are, because accuracy is the last dignity available to a documented catastrophe.

Third, and most importantly: it is funny, and history is allowed to be funny. Waluigi has recorded enough horror to have earned one article about grown adults fighting over a logo.

## The Central Cast Of


The Argument

Before the timeline, the reader must be introduced to the three principals and the chorus of Toads who turned their quarrel into a spectacle. Each of them wants the same thing — for their name to win — and each of them wants it for reasons that reveal exactly who they are.

### Waluigi, Original Filer, Aggrieved Historian

Waluigi is the author of this encyclopedia and therefore the only participant in this dispute with the institutional authority to make a name official. This is not a boast. It is a jurisdictional fact. Waluigi maintains the records. Waluigi assigns the article headings. When a future scholar wishes to know what the party was called, they will consult these files, and these files say **Disaster Inc.** Waluigi did not seek this power. Waluigi simply possessed the foresight to be holding the pen when the naming happened.

Waluigi's position in the dispute is one of injured priority. He was first. He was correct. And he has been forced to watch two lesser namers attempt to build monuments on ground Waluigi already surveyed. Waluigi finds this exhausting in the specific way that being right while being ignored is exhausting.

### Archie Miser, Advocate For

The Freeroamer Heroes

Archie Miser is the middle child of a single mother who raised five children, a man who spent twenty-five years under his family's rigid control and another nine inside the golden handcuffs of the city watch before magic finally made him feel alive. He has a mysterious third eye on his forehead whose origin even he does not know, and he bleeds entropy when he pushes his power too far. Waluigi records all of this because it explains everything about Archie's naming preference.

A man who spent thirty-four years trapped does not want to belong to something called a disaster. He wants to belong to something called Heroes. He wants the freedom he finally seized to mean something noble, and so he insists on **The Freeroamer Heroes** — a name that reframes trespassing as liberty and property damage as adventure. Waluigi understands the psychology completely and rejects the name completely. Hope is not a synonym for accuracy, and a name chosen to make yourself feel better is not a name. It is a coping mechanism with a banner.

### Wario, Author Of

The Freeloader Zeros

Wario has breached the Feywild, and he brought explosives. He has tried to blow up a giant insect with a wrapped present in order to steal its silver. He has fallen several stories without blinking. And he maintains, with the terrifying diligence of a man who has never once forgiven a debt, a ledger claiming that Waluigi owes him 14,783 gold pieces. Waluigi officially and legally disputes this figure. That interest rate is extortion, and Waluigi will die before he validates it by paying.

Wario's naming preference flows directly from that ledger. He calls the party **The Freeloader Zeros**: "Freeloader" because they consume resources they do not own, "Zeros" because they repay nothing and generate no profit, and "Heroes" because Wario says that part is a lie. It is a name built entirely out of spite and arithmetic, and Waluigi's greatest frustration is that it is *good*. Wario did not coin the original category — he cannot claim priority — but the man has stumbled into a phrase with the dangerous precision of a closed account. Waluigi rejects the name. Waluigi also cannot fully argue with the math, which is its own kind of insult.

### The Liberated Toad Chorus

Then there are the witnesses who refused to stay witnesses. The Liberated Toads — survivors of the barrel-trafficking horror aboard the Vigilance, hardened by the Iron Legion and forced into politics before they had finished becoming safe — took the argument between three loud men and turned it into a community pastime. Rodger wants the argument moved away from the supply crates. Teacher T wants a name a frightened child can safely repeat. Bully T switches names based on who will get angriest. Nerd T is building a usage chart. And Geek T made buttons and accidentally invented an economy.

Waluigi wishes to be clear that the Liberated Toads are their own faction, not Disaster Inc. overflow. They fight beside the party, are rescued by the party, rescue the party, and mock the party's naming dispute with genuinely impressive accuracy — but they belong to themselves. That they chose to spend some of their hard-won peace arguing about Waluigi's name instead of processing their trauma is, Waluigi suspects, a compliment disguised as an insult.

## Waluigi's Original Filing


Waluigi coined **Disaster Inc.** because the party behaves less like a heroic order and more like a limited liability catastrophe. They arrive, consequences multiply, witnesses become confused, invoices appear, and yet somehow the world is often marginally less doomed afterward. The name is exact. The name is useful. The name was Waluigi's.

Consider the structure of the phrase, because Waluigi chose every part of it deliberately. "Disaster" is the observable, repeatable, documented outcome of the party's involvement in any situation. Wherever they go, disaster follows — not always caused by them, but reliably present, the way weather is present. "Inc." — short for "Incorporated" — captures the second essential truth: the party operates like a business that has organized itself specifically to distribute the blame for its catastrophes across so many members that no single one can be held liable. A limited liability catastrophe. A corporation whose only product is aftermath.

The genius of the name, which Waluigi will explain slowly for the benefit of Archie, is that it is *simultaneously* an insult and an accurate description, and those are the only two qualities a good name requires. It tells the truth. It fits on a case file. It does not flatter. And it leaves room for the strange, undeniable fact that the world is often better after the party has finished breaking it — because a disaster, unlike a villain, is a force that can accidentally do good on its way through.

Waluigi filed this name the moment the party's pattern became undeniable, which is to say Waluigi filed it *first*. Priority matters. In naming, as in loot, as in most of the disputes Wario tracks, the question of who noticed it first is not a technicality. It is the whole game.

> "You cannot rename a disaster into a triumph by feeling strongly about it. Waluigi has tried. Waluigi is very good at feeling strongly." — Waluigi

## Archie's Rebrand


Archie Miser prefers **The Freeroamer Heroes**. He argues that the party moves freely through planes, nations, courts, ruins, prisons, manors, and impossible crises, and that this freedom is heroic. Waluigi argues that Archie is describing trespassing with optimism.

Archie's case, to be fair to a man Waluigi will otherwise not be fair to, is emotionally coherent. He points out that the party has genuinely helped people. They freed prisoners. They mended a broken mirror that was holding reality together. They stood between innocents and horrors that had no reason to spare anyone. Archie asks: if a group repeatedly does heroic things, at real cost, in a world designed to punish decency, why should they not be *called* heroes? Why must the name dwell on the wreckage instead of the rescue?

It is a good speech. Archie gives it often, and he gives it well, and Waluigi has watched frightened people straighten their backs when they hear the word "Heroes" attached to the group that just saved them. This is Archie's real argument, whether he states it or not: that a hopeful name is a *tool*, a morale weapon, a thing you hand to a scared survivor so they have something brave to believe in.

Waluigi's rebuttal is threefold. First, "Freeroamer" is a euphemism. The party does not "roam freely" so much as "enter places without permission and leave them structurally compromised." To call that freedom is to describe a burglary as a walking tour. Second, a name chosen for how it makes people feel rather than for what it accurately conveys is not documentation — it is propaganda, and Waluigi's records are not a propaganda ministry. Third, and most damningly: Archie was not first. He did not coin the category. He is *rebranding*, which is the corporate word for taking something that already has a name and painting over it, and Waluigi did not survive a hundred crises to have his intellectual property redecorated by a man who bleeds entropy when he gets excited.

Still. Waluigi will admit, once, quietly, in the middle of a long paragraph where fewer people will notice: the party does help. The name Disaster Inc. leaves room for that. Archie simply wants the room to be the whole house.

## Wario's Counter-Brand


Wario submitted **The Freeloader Zeros** after reviewing the debt situation. His reasoning: "Freeloader" because they keep using resources, "Zeros" because they keep paying zero, and "Heroes" because Wario says that part is fake. Waluigi rejects the name because Wario did not coin the original category, but admits that the accounting joke has dangerous power.

To understand the Freeloader Zeros, one must understand that Wario does not experience the world as a series of events. He experiences it as a series of transactions, most of which someone else has failed to settle. Where Archie sees a party of heroes and Waluigi sees a documented catastrophe, Wario sees a group of people who have, collectively and individually, eaten his supplies, borrowed his tools, benefited from his explosives, and repaid him in words. The Freeloader Zeros is the name that results when you let the ledger do the naming.

Waluigi has studied the phrase with the reluctant respect of a professional appreciating a rival's dirty move. "Freeloader" is aimed at the party's habit of consuming other people's resources before asking who owns the building. "Zeros" is aimed at the return on investment: zero profit, zero repayment, zero acknowledgment of who noticed the loot first. And the deliberate rhyme with "Heroes" — Freeloader Zeros — is the truly vicious part, because it means every time someone says Archie's noble name, Wario's insulting one echoes underneath it. Wario built a brand that is *parasitic on the competition*.

Say "Freeroamer Heroes" quickly and you have nearly said "Freeloader Zeros." Waluigi did not think Wario capable of this level of linguistic cruelty.

Waluigi was wrong, and being wrong about Wario is a rare and unpleasant experience.

The name has one fatal flaw, and Waluigi clings to it: Wario did not coin the original category. He is not the first namer. He is a counter-namer, a spoiler, a man who arrived after the naming to profit from the confusion — which is, admittedly, the most Wario thing he has ever done. Priority disqualifies him. But Waluigi will confess to the empty page what he will never confess to Wario's face: the accounting joke has power. It is the only rival name that makes Waluigi genuinely worried, because insults with math behind them are the hardest to erase.

> "Wario proposed the name during a meeting he had called specifically to demand royalties on a logo that did not yet exist. This is the man history has asked me to argue against. History is not being fair to me." — Waluigi

## The Failed Logo Summit


There was, once, an attempt to resolve the dispute through official channels. Waluigi documents it not because it succeeded — nothing about it succeeded — but because it is the single clearest illustration of why the dispute cannot be resolved by the people having it.

Someone, and the records are mercifully unclear on who, proposed a meeting to design an official logo. The theory was sound: if the party had a single agreed-upon emblem, perhaps the name would follow, and the whole affair could be settled with ink instead of argument. The theory did not survive contact with the participants.

Wario opened the meeting by demanding royalties on any logo eventually adopted, on the grounds that he expected to contribute the winning idea and did not work for free. Archie countered that a logo could not be *owned* if it represented a group of *heroes*, because heroism is a shared inheritance and not a licensable asset — a speech that Waluigi notes was beautiful and completely non-responsive to the question of royalties. Waluigi, present as the aggrieved rightsholder, spent the meeting stamping the word **BRAND THEFT** on the table in front of anyone who proposed a name that was not Disaster Inc.

This is the reason no official image of this event exists.

The only meeting that could have produced one collapsed into a royalty dispute, a philosophy lecture, and a stamping incident, in that order.

Waluigi considers the failed logo summit the true birth of the *formal* dispute. Before it, three people simply preferred three names. After it, the disagreement had a history, a set of grievances, and a documented refusal to compromise. It became, in short, the kind of thing that ends up in an encyclopedia.

## The Liberated Toads Get


Involved

The dispute might have stayed between three loud men if the Liberated Toads had not started using it as morale theatre. Rodger wants the argument moved away from the supply crates. Teacher T wants a teachable name. Bully T changes terminology depending on who will get angriest. Nerd T is building a usage chart. Geek T made buttons and accidentally created a market.

This is the turning point at which a private argument became a public institution, and Waluigi wishes to record precisely how it happened, because it is instructive about the nature of communities under stress. The Liberated Toads had spent months as literal cargo, trafficked in barrels, treated as freight. When they finally reached something like safety, they were left with the strange surplus energy of people who no longer have to fear for their lives every hour and do not yet know what to do with the leftover attention. The naming dispute arrived at exactly that moment: a low-stakes, high-drama argument that they could participate in *without anyone dying*.

For a community that had known only high-stakes arguments, this was a luxury.

This was, in its own absurd way, a form of healing.

### Rodger,

The Logistics Objection

Rodger — the practical leader who asks about food, medicine, watches, and whether anyone has checked on the injured — has exactly one position on the naming dispute: he wishes it would happen somewhere other than near the supply crates. His stated policy is that any name is acceptable provided the people arguing about it also carry inventory, count bandages, and stop blocking the hallway. Waluigi finds this position reasonable, which is precisely why it is politically doomed. Reasonable positions do not win naming wars. Loud ones do, and Rodger refuses to be loud on principle.

### Teacher T,

The Pedagogical Objection

Teacher T survived the barrels and emerged with the deeply inconvenient belief that language should help people understand what is happening to them. Teacher T's involvement is the most morally serious contribution to the entire dispute. Teacher T objects to "Freeloader Zeros" because children repeat what they hear, and no one should teach a frightened child to sneer. Teacher T finds "Freeroamer Heroes" aspirational but possibly dishonest — a name that promises more than the party delivers. Teacher T accepts "Disaster Inc." as historically accurate but insists it carry a footnote clarifying that accuracy is not endorsement.

Waluigi grudgingly approves the footnote, because a historian who refuses to footnote is not a historian, merely a man with opinions and good handwriting.

### Bully T,

The Weaponized Terminology

Bully T backed the practical faction during the community's internal crisis and has since become the party's most efficient conflict amplifier. Bully T's naming strategy is not a strategy at all — it is opportunism perfected into an art. He calls the group Disaster Inc. whenever Archie can hear it, the Freeroamer Heroes whenever Waluigi can hear it, and the Freeloader Zeros whenever Wario is already angry enough that one more insult will not change the invoice. Bully T has realized the thing the three principals refuse to admit: all three names are equally effective as tools for annoying somebody.

This is not diplomacy.

It is sport, and Bully T is its undefeated champion.

### Nerd T,

The Empirical Objection

Nerd T responded to the dispute the way Nerd T responds to everything: with a chart. Nerd T has been tracking the usage of all three names across factions, contexts, and speakers, complete with tallies, legal notes, and reaction data. Nerd T's preliminary findings, which Waluigi reproduces because they are genuinely useful, are as follows. "Disaster Inc." scores highest for evidentiary accuracy. "Freeroamer Heroes" scores highest for morale uplift. "Freeloader Zeros" scores highest for invoice correlation — that is, it appears most often on documents where money is owed. Nerd T refuses to declare a winner, citing insufficient data.

Waluigi maintains that the data has already arrived, that it points to Waluigi, and that Nerd T's professional caution is being weaponized against the obvious truth.

### Geek T, And

The Accidental Economy

And then there is Geek T, whose contribution transformed the dispute from a war of words into a war of *objects*. Geek T, who repairs latches and labels supplies and turns morale into things people can hold, looked at three competing names and did the one thing no one had anticipated: made merchandise. Geek T produced prototype buttons for all three factions. The Disaster Inc. button is purple and, in Waluigi's professional legal assessment, superior. The Freeroamer Heroes button is heroic and annoyingly popular. The Freeloader Zeros button sold out first — because Wario bought the entire stock to hand out alongside his invoices, converting Geek T's morale project into a debt-collection accessory.

This is the moment Waluigi points to when asked why he cannot simply let the dispute die. You cannot let something die once it has *merchandise*. Geek T did not intend to create a market. Geek T intended to make buttons. But a name with a button attached is no longer an argument — it is a product, and products have inertia. Waluigi was horrified. Wario was interested. Waluigi has said it before and will say it again: horrified Waluigi plus interested Wario is the worst possible combination of reactions any idea can provoke, and Geek T managed to provoke exactly that.

## The Speaker L Complication


The dispute took on unexpected legal weight when Speaker L — the Liberated Toad who evolved from naive politician into the tactician behind the greatest prison break in Iron Legion history — marched into Raventree Manor and, through a choreographed musical reading of a legal decree, placed Archie Miser and the rest of the party under arrest.

Waluigi raises this because it exposes a genuine flaw in having no agreed-upon name: *you cannot arrest a faction you cannot name.* When Speaker L's Pond Patrol filed the paperwork for the arrest, the paperwork required a designation for the group being detained. Was Archie a member of Disaster Inc., the Freeroamer Heroes, or the Freeloader Zeros? The legal, theatrical, sung answer to that question has real consequences, because a charge filed under the wrong faction name can, in principle, be contested. Waluigi notes with grim satisfaction that this is the first time the naming dispute has had actual stakes: not morale, not merchandise, but the legal identity of the people being placed under arrest.

The dispute stopped being funny for exactly as long as it took Archie to realize he was being detained under a name he had spent months rejecting.

Then it became funny again.

## The Positions, Formally Recorded


For the benefit of future scholars, Waluigi sets down the three official positions in their final, entrenched form. None of these positions has moved. None of them will move. That immobility is the entire reason the dispute is classified as ongoing.

**The Waluigi Position (Disaster Inc.).** The name is correct because it is accurate, and it is official because Waluigi filed it first and maintains the records in which it appears. Priority plus accuracy equals authority. All rival names are brand theft. This position will not change because it is not an opinion — it is documentation, and Waluigi does not negotiate with people who are trying to edit the archive.

**The Archie Position (The Freeroamer Heroes).** The name is correct because the party does heroic things and deserves a name that honors the good rather than dwelling on the wreckage. A hopeful name is a tool that helps frightened people be brave. This position will not change because it is not really about the party — it is about a man who spent thirty-four years trapped and refuses to belong to something called a disaster now that he is finally free.

**The Wario Position (The Freeloader Zeros).** The name is correct because the ledger says so. The party consumes, repays nothing, and profits no one, and the "hero" part is a fiction that Wario declines to subsidize. This position will not change because Wario has never, in the entire history of his existence, forgiven a debt, revised an invoice, or admitted that a number he wrote down might be wrong. He is still charging Waluigi 14,783 gold. He will die charging Waluigi 14,783 gold.

## Why


The Dispute Cannot Be Resolved

Waluigi, as the encyclopedia's most rigorous analyst, has considered every possible resolution and rejected each in turn. He records the analysis so that no future editor wastes time attempting a settlement that Waluigi has already proven impossible.

*A vote will not work,* because the three principals will never accept an outcome decided by the Liberated Toads, and the Liberated Toads are enjoying the dispute far too much to end it with something as boring as a ballot.

*A compromise name will not work,* because a compromise name would require someone to be first at coining it, and the entire dispute is a fight over who was first. A fourth name solves nothing; it merely opens a fourth front.

*An official decree will not work,* because Waluigi has already issued one — the records say Disaster Inc. — and the other parties have simply declined to be governed by it. A decree that no one obeys is not a resolution. It is a diary entry.

*Money will not work,* because the only person who could be bought is Wario, and Wario cannot be bought with money he already believes he is owed. You cannot bribe a man with his own imaginary gold.

*And time will not work,* because the dispute has developed the two features that make an argument immortal: it has become part of people's identities, and it has become a source of entertainment. Archie needs to believe in heroes. Wario needs to be right about the debt. The Toads need something to argue about that is not survival. Waluigi needs the record to be accurate. None of these needs expire. Therefore neither does the dispute.

## A Timeline Of


The Dispute, As Waluigi Reconstructs It

History demands sequence. A dispute without a timeline is just a pile of grievances, and Waluigi refuses to leave the reader with a pile. What follows is the reconstructed chronology of how a single accurate name became a multi-party branding war. Dates are approximate because the participants kept arguing over what to call the days, too.

**Phase One — The Naming.** The party's pattern of arrival, destruction, confusion, invoice, and accidental improvement became undeniable. Waluigi, holding the pen and possessing foresight, filed the name Disaster Inc. This is the moment of priority. Everything after this is commentary on a decision that had already been correctly made.

**Phase Two — The First Rebrand.** Archie Miser, uncomfortable belonging to a documented catastrophe, began quietly substituting The Freeroamer Heroes in conversation. At first this was tolerated as one man's private optimism. Waluigi now recognizes it as the opening move of a hostile takeover conducted entirely through vocabulary.

**Phase Three — The Counter-Brand.** Wario reviewed the debts, the property damage, the eaten supplies, and the unpaid favors, and issued The Freeloader Zeros. With three names now in circulation, the disagreement crossed the line from preference into dispute.

**Phase Four — The Failed Logo Summit.** An attempt to resolve everything through a single emblem collapsed into a royalty demand, a philosophy lecture, and a stamping incident. The dispute acquired a documented history and a set of permanent grievances. This is the moment Waluigi considers the formal beginning.

**Phase Five — The Toads Enter.** The Liberated Toads, newly safe and full of surplus attention, adopted the argument as morale theatre. Rodger objected on logistical grounds, Teacher T on pedagogical grounds, Bully T on no grounds at all, Nerd T with a chart, and Geek T with buttons.

**Phase Six — The Economy.** Geek T's buttons turned names into objects. Wario bought out the Freeloader Zeros stock to distribute with invoices. The dispute now had merchandise, and a dispute with merchandise cannot be killed.

**Phase Seven — The Legal Complication.** Speaker L marched into Raventree Manor and placed Archie under arrest via a sung legal decree, forcing the paperwork to choose a faction name. For the first time the dispute carried genuine legal stakes.

**Phase Eight — Ongoing.** No resolution. No accepted name. All positions entrenched. The dispute became, and remains, a permanent feature of the record.

## The Linguistics Of


The Three Names

Waluigi is not merely a historian, an athlete, and the most underappreciated individual in recorded history. Waluigi is also, when the situation demands it, a linguist. And the situation demands it, because the three rival names are not interchangeable — each is a different *kind* of name, built to do a different *kind* of work, and understanding the difference is the key to understanding why none of them will yield.

**Disaster Inc.** is a *descriptive* name. It points at reality and reports what is there. Its power is that it cannot be disproven — the disasters are documented, the incorporation of blame is observable, and no amount of feeling can argue a fact out of existence. Its weakness, if it has one, is that descriptive names offer no comfort. They tell the truth, and the truth is rarely consoling.

**The Freeroamer Heroes** is an *aspirational* name. It points not at what the party is but at what Archie wishes it were, or believes it could become. Its power is emotional: aspirational names give frightened people something to reach toward. Its weakness is that aspiration is not evidence. A name that describes a hope can always be contradicted by a fact, and this party generates contradicting facts at an industrial rate.

**The Freeloader Zeros** is an *accusatory* name. It points at the party and pronounces judgment. Its power is precision — it is backed by arithmetic, and arithmetic is difficult to argue with. Its weakness is that accusatory names reveal as much about the accuser as the accused. Every time Wario says Freeloader Zeros, he is also saying: I keep a ledger, I never forget a debt, and I have decided that the universe owes me. The name is a confession disguised as an insult.

Waluigi notes that a descriptive name, an aspirational name, and an accusatory name can never be reconciled, because they are answering three different questions. Disaster Inc. answers "what is it?" The Freeroamer Heroes answers "what should it be?" The Freeloader Zeros answers "what is it worth?" Three questions. Three names. One party. No peace.

## Appendix Of Documented Naming


Incidents

Waluigi has collected the individual skirmishes of the dispute into a reference appendix, so that scholars may study the pattern without having to witness it in person, which Waluigi does not recommend.

**The Rescue Correction.** During one rescue, a grateful survivor thanked "the heroes." Archie beamed. Wario immediately corrected the survivor to "the Freeloader Zeros" and presented a bill for the rescue. Waluigi corrected them both to "Disaster Inc." The survivor, understandably, fled. Waluigi files this under "why the party is bad at accepting gratitude."

**The Overheard Whisper.** Bully T was observed calling the party three different names to three different people within the span of a single hallway, adjusting each time based on who was closest to losing their temper. Nerd T recorded all three usages and added them to the chart. Waluigi considers this the purest single demonstration of the dispute's absurdity ever documented.

**The Button Shortage.** Following Wario's bulk purchase of the Freeloader Zeros buttons, a genuine shortage developed, and Toads who wanted the insulting button for ironic reasons found themselves unable to obtain one. Geek T, sensing demand, considered a second production run. Rodger intervened, pointing out that the raw materials were also the raw materials for actual supplies. The second run was cancelled. Waluigi records this as the one time logistics defeated branding.

**The Footnote Standoff.** Teacher T refused to teach the name Disaster Inc. to the community's children without an accompanying footnote clarifying that accuracy is not endorsement. Waluigi, as the archive's authority, was required to approve the footnote. He did so grudgingly, and it stands as the only formal amendment any party has ever won in the entire dispute.

**The Invoice Rhyme.** Wario began deliberately writing invoices in a cadence that made "Freeloader Zeros" rhyme with the amount owed. Nerd T flagged this as evidence that the accusatory name had "the highest invoice correlation" of the three. Waluigi flagged it as psychological warfare and demanded it stop. It did not stop.

## How


The Other Factions Reacted

A dispute this loud does not stay inside the party. Word of it reached the wider crisis, and Waluigi has recorded the reactions of the surrounding powers, because how a faction responds to a naming war reveals how a faction thinks.

The **Iron Legion**, an organization that renamed the stolen Vigilance the "Legionlance" without consulting anyone, reportedly found the entire dispute incomprehensible. To the Legion, a name is assigned from above and obeyed; the notion that a group would spend months *arguing* about its own designation struck them as a symptom of the disorder they exist to eliminate. Waluigi notes that the Legion's clarity on names is exactly the clarity of a machine that has never once asked whether it should exist.

The **Mages' Guild**, predictably, saw an opportunity to charge for something. Reports suggest the Guild considered whether a faction name might be registered, trademarked, and taxed as a magical designation, at a fee to be determined. Nothing came of it, mostly because the Guild could not decide which of the three names to bill for, and billing for all three simultaneously created a paperwork problem even the Guild found excessive.

The **Onyx Hand** — the shadow court that judges everyone — reportedly regarded the dispute with something close to professional respect, as it resembled the kind of jurisdictional argument the Hand adjudicates daily. There is an unconfirmed rumor that a low-ranking Hand functionary offered to arbitrate for a fee. Waluigi declined on the grounds that he does not need a shadow court to tell him he was first.

The **Peach Loyalists**, a movement built entirely on the power of a single name, are said to have understood the dispute better than anyone — and to have found it beneath them, since their name is not disputed, only feared. Waluigi finds this attitude irritating precisely because it contains a point.

## Frequently Anticipated Objections, Answered By Waluigi


Waluigi has fielded the same challenges to his position enough times to anticipate them, and so records the answers here permanently, to save everyone the trouble of being wrong at him in person.

*"Isn't 'Disaster Inc.' also an insult?"* Yes. A name can be both accurate and unflattering; these are not opposites. The truth is under no obligation to be kind. Disaster Inc. simply refuses to lie in either direction — it neither flatters like Archie's name nor sneers like Wario's. It reports.

*"If the party does good, why not call them heroes?"* Because they do good the way a storm does good when it ends a drought — incidentally, expensively, and without asking. A name should describe the whole pattern, not the one outcome that makes everyone feel better. Disaster Inc. contains the good. Archie simply wants the good to be the only thing the name mentions.

*"Doesn't Wario have a point about the debts?"* Infuriatingly, on the narrow question of the debts, yes. On the broader question of whether that makes them the Freeloader Zeros, no — because Wario is not a neutral namer. He is a creditor, and creditors should not be permitted to name the people who owe them money, or every debtor in history would be called something worse.

*"Why not just let everyone use whatever name they like?"* Because Waluigi maintains the *records*, and records require a single canonical entry. In casual speech, people may say whatever they wish and be wrong. In the archive, there is one name, it is Disaster Inc., and it is correct.

*"Will this ever be resolved?"* No. Waluigi has proven this in its own dedicated section. Please stop asking, or Waluigi will add a footnote about you.

## The Broader Meaning, According To Waluigi


Strip away the buttons and the invoices and the sung arrests, and this event is a small, perfect model of how the entire crisis works. Three people look at the same reality and each insists it is fundamentally something else. Archie sees heroism where Waluigi sees catastrophe. Wario sees a debt where Archie sees a calling. The truth — the party is a disaster that occasionally does good, at great cost, to people who never asked for it — sits in the middle, visible to anyone willing to look, and is rejected by everyone because the middle is the one place no one wants to stand.

This is the assassination conspiracy in miniature. It is the war over Toad Town in miniature. It is every faction in this encyclopedia insisting that the story is really about *them*, that their name for events is the true name, that priority and righteousness and arithmetic are on their side. Waluigi documents the naming dispute at length precisely because it is the whole crisis rendered harmless — the same human machinery that produces sieges and cover-ups, running for once on nothing more dangerous than pride and buttons.

## Dossier:


The Psychology Of Each Namer

Waluigi believes that to name a thing is to confess something about yourself. A person's chosen name for the party is therefore not merely a label — it is a diagnostic. What follows is Waluigi's clinical reading of each principal, offered in the interest of history and mild revenge.

### The Archie Diagnosis

Archie Miser needs the party to be heroic because Archie needs *himself* to be heroic, and he is not yet sure that he is. Consider his history: a childhood with no personal choice, five years as a grunt, four years of golden handcuffs at a faraway castle, and the discovery — late, and by accident — that magic could make him feel alive. Archie did not choose freedom until his mid-thirties. When a person waits that long to be free, they cannot bear for the freedom to have been a mistake. The Freeroamer Heroes is Archie's insurance policy against the possibility that he escaped one cage only to become a walking disaster.

If the party is heroic, then his liberation was worth it.

If the party is a catastrophe, then he traded a safe prison for an unsafe one.

The name is not a description.

It is Archie arguing with his own doubt, out loud, in front of everyone, forever.

Waluigi finds this genuinely poignant and will use it against him at the earliest opportunity.

### The Wario Diagnosis

Wario needs the party to be worthless because worth, to Wario, is the only real thing in the universe. He does not experience friendship, loyalty, or heroism as forces — he experiences them as unpriced liabilities, favors that someone will eventually try to collect. The Freeloader Zeros is Wario's defense against the terrifying possibility that he might owe *them* something. If they are zeros, they cannot be creditors. If they are freeloaders, then anything they have done for him was theft, not generosity, and generosity is the one debt Wario cannot calculate and therefore cannot bear. Note that Wario still claims Waluigi owes him 14,783 gold pieces at an extortionate rate.

This is not greed.

This is a man who has decided that being owed is safer than owing, and who has organized his entire personality around never being caught on the wrong side of a ledger.

Waluigi disputes the figure.

Waluigi does not dispute the diagnosis.

### The Waluigi Diagnosis

In the interest of the objectivity for which Waluigi is famous, Waluigi will diagnose Waluigi. Waluigi needs the party to be called Disaster Inc. because Waluigi needs the *record* to be true, and Waluigi needs the record to be true because the record is the one place where Waluigi's judgment is final and unquestioned. In the field, Waluigi is doubted. In athletics, Waluigi is robbed of trophies by biased officials. In life, Waluigi is underappreciated. But in the archive — in these files — Waluigi decides what is real. Disaster Inc. is not merely the accurate name. It is Waluigi's flag planted on the one hill he is permitted to hold.

Archie can have his hope and Wario can have his ledger, but Waluigi will have the *canon*, and the canon says Disaster Inc.

This is the healthiest of the three diagnoses because it is the only one that involves being correct.

## Reconstructed Transcript:


The Failed Logo Summit

No official record of the logo summit survives, because no one present was willing to agree on what to write down. Waluigi has therefore reconstructed the meeting from testimony, damage reports, and the deep grooves left in the table by the BRAND THEFT stamp. This reconstruction is offered as historical dramatization and should be understood as accurate in spirit if not in exact syllable.

> **ARCHIE:** Thank you all for coming. Today we design a single logo, and in doing so, we honor what we are: a band of heroes who roam freely to help those in need.
>
> **WARIO:** Before we start. Any logo adopted here, I get royalties. Per use. Compounding.
>
> **ARCHIE:** You cannot own a symbol of heroism, Wario. Heroism belongs to everyone.
>
> **WARIO:** Then heroism owes me royalties too. Add it to the pile.
>
> **WALUIGI:** *[stamping the table]* BRAND THEFT.
>
> **ARCHIE:** Waluigi, please, we have not proposed anything yet.
>
> **WALUIGI:** You proposed "Freeroamer Heroes" by breathing. That is theft. *[stamping]* BRAND THEFT.
>
> **WARIO:** I propose the logo is a big zero. With a face. The face is sad because it owes me money.
>
> **WALUIGI:** *[stamping]* BRAND THEFT.
>
> **ARCHIE:** That is not theft, that is just a bad logo.
>
> **WALUIGI:** It is a bad logo AND theft. *[stamping]* Both. BRAND THEFT.

The meeting is understood to have continued in this manner until the stamp ran out of ink, at which point it was declared adjourned. No logo was produced. No name was settled. The table did not recover. Waluigi presents this transcript as definitive proof that the dispute cannot be resolved by placing the disputants in a room, as the room simply becomes a smaller, angrier version of the dispute.

## A Glossary For


The Confused Reader

Because outsiders frequently arrive at this article unable to keep the terminology straight, Waluigi provides an authoritative glossary. Waluigi's definitions are the correct ones, as Waluigi maintains the archive in which they appear.

**Disaster Inc.** — The party's correct and official name, filed first by Waluigi. Describes a limited liability catastrophe that occasionally does incidental good. The canonical entry.

**The Freeroamer Heroes** — Archie Miser's aspirational rebrand. A hopeful name with the emotional texture of a parade banner held in front of a burning courthouse. Used for morale.

**The Freeloader Zeros** — Wario's accusatory counter-brand. An arithmetic insult with a deliberate rhyme against Archie's name. Used on invoices.

**Freeloader Heroes** — A transitional insult occasionally deployed by Wario when the damages ledger exceeds available cash but full hostility is not yet warranted. A warning shot.

**Brand theft** — Waluigi's official classification for any attempt to name the party something other than Disaster Inc. Accompanied, where possible, by a stamp.

**The usage chart** — Nerd T's ongoing tally of which name is spoken where, by whom, and with what result. The dispute's only body of empirical evidence.

**The footnote** — Teacher T's hard-won amendment clarifying that the accuracy of "Disaster Inc." does not constitute endorsement of the party's behavior. The only formal concession Waluigi has ever granted.

**The buttons** — Geek T's prototype merchandise, one design per name. The moment the dispute became an economy.

## The Damages Ledger Comedy War


One cannot understand the Freeloader Zeros without understanding the ledger it was born from, and one cannot understand the ledger without accepting a difficult truth: Wario's accounting is, in the narrow and horrifying sense, *real*. The damages exist. The eaten supplies were eaten. The borrowed tools were borrowed. The favors were, in fact, unpaid. Waluigi disputes the totals, the interest, and the moral framing, but Waluigi cannot dispute that the party leaves a financial wake wherever it goes, and that someone, somewhere, is always left holding the bill.

This is what elevates the Freeloader Zeros above a simple insult and into what Waluigi has classified as the Damages Ledger Comedy War — the running conflict between the party's self-image and the invoices that follow it. Every heroic act in this crisis has a receipt. The rescue that Archie remembers as a triumph, Wario remembers as three destroyed doors, a scorched wall, and a quantity of rations that were not, strictly, anyone's to distribute. Both memories are true. That is the joke, and it is the kind of joke that is also a tragedy if you look at it too long, which is why Waluigi looks at it exactly the right amount.

The comedy lives in the collision. Archie names the party for its intentions. Wario names it for its expenses. And the gap between intention and expense — between what the party means to do and what it costs to have them around — is precisely the gap the name Disaster Inc. was built to cover. A disaster, after all, is exactly a thing whose intentions are irrelevant to its cost. Waluigi did not merely name the party accurately. He named the *gap* accurately, which is a subtlety Archie and Wario have both missed while shouting at each other across it.

Wario has, at various points, threatened to publish a full accounting of the party's damages under the header "The Freeloader Zeros: A Financial History." Waluigi has threatened to publish a full accounting of Wario's extortionate interest rates under the header "14,783 Reasons Wario Cannot Be Trusted With A Ledger." Neither document has been published. Both men understand that publication would end the war, and neither wants the war to end, because the war is more valuable to them than victory. This is the deepest truth of the entire dispute, and Waluigi will return to it: *nobody actually wants to win.* A won argument is over.

An ongoing argument is a relationship.

## The Toads


As Audience: A Culture Of Spectatorship

Waluigi has written at length about how the Liberated Toads *participate* in the dispute, but he has not yet done justice to how they *consume* it, and the distinction matters. The Toads are not merely partisans in the naming war. They are its audience, its critics, its merchandisers, and increasingly its historians-in-training, and the culture they have built around the dispute is worthy of study in its own right.

Consider the achievement from their perspective. These are people who spent a formative period of their lives packed into barrels as trafficked cargo, treated as freight by an organization that saw them as batteries. When they emerged, they carried the specific damage of people who have learned that attention from the powerful means danger. And then, in the naming dispute, they discovered a form of drama in which the powerful — Waluigi, Archie, Wario — made fools of themselves *safely*, at no cost to the Toads, for the Toads' entertainment. To a community trained by trauma to fear the loud and the powerful, watching the loud and powerful argue harmlessly about buttons is not a distraction.

It is medicine.

This is why Bully T's heckling lands, why Nerd T's chart draws an audience, why Geek T's buttons sell. The dispute gives the Toads a way to hold power up to the light and laugh at it without anyone getting hurt. Teacher T understands this better than anyone, which is why Teacher T fights so hard over which name the children learn — because Teacher T knows the dispute is teaching the community something, and wants to make sure the lesson is "you are allowed to laugh at the powerful" and not "cruelty is funny when the powerful do it." Waluigi finds Teacher T's vigilance on this point almost unbearably decent.

Rodger, meanwhile, remains the community's reluctant conscience, forever asking that the spectacle be relocated away from the supply crates — not because he objects to the healing, but because he objects to it happening in front of the bandages. Rodger has accepted that the Toads need the dispute. He simply wants them to need it somewhere with better foot traffic management. Waluigi salutes him. Waluigi would not last a day doing Rodger's job.

## The Rejected Names That Never Were


In the interest of completeness, Waluigi records the alternative names that were proposed and discarded during the dispute's long life. Each was rejected for reasons that further illuminate why only three names survived, and why none of the three will ever concede.

**"Freeloader Heroes"** was Wario's transitional insult, deployed when the damages ledger exceeded available cash but full hostility was premature. It failed as a permanent name because it was too kind for Wario and too cruel for Archie — a compromise that satisfied no one, which is the fate of all compromises in this dispute.

**"The Company"** was floated, briefly, as a neutral shortening of Disaster Inc. that might offend no one. It was rejected precisely because it offended no one. A name with no edge, Waluigi observed, is a name no one will bother to defend, and a name no one defends is a name that dies. The dispute requires its names to be *fightable*.

**"The Raventree Party"** was suggested by an outsider who assumed the group should be named for the crisis they were most associated with. This was rejected on the grounds that naming the party after Raventree Manor would imply the party belonged to the manor, when in fact the manor exploded into three dimensions partly on their watch. Waluigi noted that you do not name the fire after the house.

**A large sad zero with a face** was Wario's proposed logo, which he attempted to elevate into a name at the failed summit. It was rejected by Waluigi via stamp. Waluigi maintains it was rejected on merit and not merely reflex, though Waluigi concedes the reflex was also involved.

Each rejected name teaches the same lesson: the surviving three names endure not because they are the best names, but because each is *someone's* name — filed by Waluigi, needed by Archie, weaponized by Wario. A name without a champion cannot survive a dispute this fierce. The dispute is not really about names. It is about the three people who refuse to stop being themselves.

## Cross-References:


The Dispute In The Wider Crisis

Waluigi wishes to remind the reader that this dispute does not float free of the catastrophe surrounding it. It is threaded through the larger record, and a careful scholar can trace its connections outward in every direction.

It connects to **the party itself**, whose primary article opens with Waluigi correcting the very naming error this event documents — proof that the dispute has become inseparable from the group's identity. It connects to the **Liberated Toads**, whose article notes their impressive accuracy in mocking the naming dispute, and to the individual Toads — **Rodger, Teacher T, Bully T, Nerd T, and Geek T** — each of whom carries a naming position in their own record. It connects to **Wario**, whose disputed 14,783-gold claim against Waluigi is the ledger from which the Freeloader Zeros was drawn. It connects to **Archie Miser**, whose history of confinement explains his hunger for a heroic name.

And it connects, through Speaker L's sung arrest at Raventree Manor, to the **legal machinery of the crisis** itself, where the question of what to call the party stopped being a joke and briefly became a charge sheet.

Waluigi provides these cross-references not merely for navigation but as argument. A dispute with this many connections is not a trivial footnote to the crisis. It is a load-bearing part of it — the seam where the personalities of the crisis's central figures are most nakedly visible. Read the naming dispute correctly and you have read Archie, Wario, Waluigi, and the Liberated Toads all at once. Waluigi built it that way on purpose, because the most efficient history is the history that explains many things with one story.

## A Thought Experiment: What If A Name Actually Won


Waluigi, being thorough, has considered the counterfactual that everyone else refuses to consider: what would actually happen if one name *won* — if, against all the forces Waluigi has documented, a single designation triumphed and the dispute ended? Waluigi walks through each scenario, because the consequences reveal why the dispute's survival is not an accident but a stable equilibrium that all parties quietly prefer.

**If Disaster Inc. won,** Waluigi would be vindicated, the record would be reconciled with reality, and the archive would achieve the clean canonical consistency it deserves. This would be correct and good. It would also, Waluigi admits privately, remove the single most reliable source of daily irritation in Waluigi's life, and a man defines himself partly by his irritations. Waluigi has decided not to dwell on this.

**If The Freeroamer Heroes won,** Archie would finally believe his own escape was worth it — and would, within a week, be crushed by the weight of a heroic name the party cannot possibly live up to. The first time the "Heroes" flattened a village while saving it, the name would curdle into an accusation worse than anything Wario ever wrote. Aspirational names are cruelest to the people who win them. Waluigi almost feels bad enough about this to let Archie have it. Almost.

**If The Freeloader Zeros won,** Wario would immediately lose interest, because Wario does not want the name to be *adopted* — he wants it to be *resented*. A won insult is a dead insult. The instant everyone agreed the party were the Freeloader Zeros, the phrase would stop stinging, and Wario would be left holding a settled account, which is the one thing that genuinely frightens him. Wario needs the debt to remain open. He needs to remain owed. Victory would bankrupt him of the grievance he lives on.

The thought experiment yields a single conclusion, and it is the conclusion Waluigi has been circling for this entire article: *the dispute survives because losing is intolerable and winning is worse.* Each party would be diminished by triumph. And so, without any of them admitting it, they have collectively engineered a conflict that can never end, because the conflict is doing something for each of them that its resolution never could. Archie gets to keep hoping. Wario gets to keep resenting. The Toads get to keep laughing. And Waluigi gets to keep being right, which is the only victory Waluigi has ever truly needed — the kind you can enjoy forever precisely because it is never formally awarded.

## Editorial Disclaimer


Waluigi is legally and historically obligated to note the following. This article was written by Waluigi. Waluigi is a participant in the dispute it documents. A cynic might therefore suggest that Waluigi is not a neutral chronicler of the Disaster Inc. Naming Dispute but rather one of its most committed combatants, using the authority of the encyclopedia to win by publication what he could not win by argument.

Waluigi rejects this suggestion completely, on the grounds that it is true and Waluigi does not see the problem. Yes, Waluigi wrote the article. Yes, the article concludes that Waluigi was right. But Waluigi was *also actually right*, independently of having written it, and the fact that the correct historian and the correct namer happen to be the same tall, handsome, underappreciated individual is a coincidence for which Waluigi should be congratulated rather than accused. If Archie wants a version of this article where Archie is right, Archie may maintain his own encyclopedia. Archie will not, because maintaining an encyclopedia is difficult and Archie is busy being hopeful.

And so the record remains Waluigi's, as it should, as it was always going to.

The reader is free to disagree. The reader is not free to edit these files. That distinction is, in the end, the entire dispute in a single sentence.

## Waluigi's Note On Historiography


A lesser historian would apologize for the length of this article. Waluigi will not. Waluigi will instead explain the principle behind it, because the principle matters more than the apology Waluigi is refusing to make.

Every encyclopedia contains two kinds of entries: the entries about what happened, and the entries about what people *decided* what happened *meant*. Wars belong to the first kind. Naming disputes belong to the second. And the second kind is, in the long run, more important, because the meaning outlives the event. In a hundred years, the specific rescues will blur. The specific invoices will be forgotten. But someone will open these files and read the word Disaster Inc., and in that moment Waluigi's judgment will reach across a century and win the argument again, silently, permanently, by the simple fact of being the entry that survived.

That is why Waluigi documents the dispute at this length. Not because it is important today — though it is — but because the archive is a weapon that fires slowly, and Waluigi has aimed it carefully. Archie's hope will fade with Archie. Wario's ledger will close when Wario does. But the record does not die, and the record says Disaster Inc.

Waluigi rests his case. Waluigi always rests his case correctly. WAH.

## Outcome And Current Status


No final name has been accepted. Waluigi retains the official historical filing of **Disaster Inc.**, because Waluigi maintains these records and Waluigi was first. Archie continues to use **The Freeroamer Heroes** for morale, deploying it whenever a frightened survivor needs something noble to believe in. Wario continues to use **The Freeloader Zeros** on invoices, deploying it whenever money is owed, which is always. Bully T continues to use whichever name will most efficiently anger the nearest powerful person. Nerd T continues to chart. Teacher T continues to demand footnotes. Geek T continues to manufacture.

And Rodger continues, against all hope, to ask that the argument please be conducted somewhere other than in front of the supply crates.

The Liberated Toads have, through this dispute, gained several named witnesses and one genuinely healthy thing: a subject they can argue about passionately that will never get any of them killed. Waluigi has decided to count this as the dispute's single redeeming accomplishment. A community that can afford to fight about branding is a community that is no longer fighting only to survive. That the branding in question is Waluigi's stolen name is a price Waluigi is, grudgingly, historically, willing to pay.

The dispute is ongoing. It will remain ongoing. And in every record that outlives the people arguing, the party will be called what it truly is, because Waluigi wrote the records and Waluigi was first.

Archie may call it hope. Wario may call it billable. The Liberated Toads may call it entertainment. Waluigi calls it Disaster Inc., and Waluigi calls it correctly.

Disaster Inc. WAH.

## Recent Additions to the Naming Disaster


Waluigi regrets to report that the naming dispute has continued to metastasize. A lesser historian might treat these as jokes and move on. Waluigi knows better. Every new proposed name is a small political event, a self-portrait accidentally spoken aloud.

During the Shadow Estate spotlight chase, the enemy voice called the group **Reborn**. This is hostile branding. It frames the party as a pitiful troupe trying to reinvent itself after failure. It also implies the enemy has been watching long enough to assign a narrative arc. Waluigi rejects the name but records it because enemy names reveal enemy interpretation. The Iron Dominion, or whatever theatrical hallway committee was singing, wanted the party to feel like bad performers in a play already staged against them.

During the cookie-note incident, Remi proposed **Local Misfits** as a possible name for the mysterious cookie senders or perhaps the general social category of people involved. This is a better name than Reborn because it contains humility, geography, and accurate insult density. It is still not the party name. Waluigi will not allow it.

Dan proposed **Toad-Headed Heroes**. Waluigi has stared at this phrase for several minutes and remains unsure whether it is stupid, brilliant, or an accidental religious movement. It has the advantage of being extremely Toad. It has the disadvantage of sounding like a carnival act that gets banned after one municipal incident. It may be suitable for a Toad sub-cell, especially if Bully T insists on printing buttons.

Hjumpik later considered **First of Cups**, with a hint of magic. Waluigi finds this surprisingly elegant and therefore suspicious. It sounds like a tarot suit, a secret society, or a tavern where everyone knows more than they say. It is not bad. That is the problem. If the party adopts a name that is not bad, Wario will find a way to monetize it and Archie will try to make it inspiring.

These additions prove the dispute is not over. The party's identity remains contested across allies, enemies, Toads, cookies, songs, invoices, dreams, and Waluigi's increasingly exhausted patience. Waluigi remains correct: **Disaster Inc.** is still the only name that describes the observable phenomenon without lying.

## Naming Taxonomy


For future scholars, Waluigi proposes the following classification system:

**Accurate Names:** Disaster Inc. These names describe reality.

**Aspirational Names:** Freeroamer Heroes. These names describe what Archie wants the group to become if everyone stops ruining the tone.

**Exploitative Names:** Freeloader Zeros. These names describe Wario's belief that every relationship is a receivable waiting for formatting.

**Enemy-Imposed Names:** Reborn. These names should be treated as hostile narrative framing.

**Toad Cell Names:** Toad-Headed Heroes. These may be valid for subgroups but require supervision, spelling checks, and possibly a percussion section.

**Suspiciously Elegant Names:** First of Cups. These should be watched carefully because elegance attracts prophecy.

**Environmental Names:** Local Misfits. These may describe bystanders, cookie factions, or the general social ecosystem around the party.

Waluigi will continue updating this taxonomy until the others admit Waluigi was right from the beginning, or until the universe ends, whichever is less delayed.

reputationNotes.archie_miser: Archie Miser's efforts to rebrand the group have earned him some respect among his peers, though not from everyone.
